sentences.text: Specimens of Nanosaurus measured between 2 and 2.2 meters in length and weighed between 20 and 30 kilograms.
The animal possessed short, broad hands with short fingers.
Its mouth contained small, leaf-shaped cheek teeth with ridges and denticles, while the premaxillary teeth were less ornamented.
Nanosaurus had thin, cartilaginous intercostal plates running along its ribs, a trait shared with other neornithischians.
Nanosaurus was a very small dinosaur compared to the giant sauropods found in the same area.
Othniel Charles Marsh originally described the species as being fox-sized.
Fossils of Nanosaurus have been found in the Morrison Formation of the south-western United States.
The species Nanosaurus agilis was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1877.
There are 32 recorded fossil occurrences of Nanosaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
While typically viewed as a small, fast herbivore, some researchers like Bakker in 1986 suggested Nanosaurus was an omnivore.
Nanosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
The genus belongs to the parent group Neornithischia.
Modern research classifies Nanosaurus as a basal member of the Neornithischia clade.
Fossils of Nanosaurus have been found in stratigraphic zones 2 through 5 of the Morrison Formation.
A 2025 study argued that the type specimens of Nanosaurus and related genera are too fragmentary to confirm they represent the same animal, suggesting they should remain as nomina dubia.
